messages:
zara-peopleops: Quick Q from Mike: Leo has an approved level change (L2 -> L3) with an effective date of 2026-11-01 but he's scheduled to be on an unpaid leave from 2026-11-10 to 2026-11-30. Mike asked whether we should still retro to 11/01 and how leave affects proration and benefits.
mike-engmgr: We want the new comp to reflect 11/01 for offer comps and internal parity. Is retro still straightforward if part of the retro window overlaps unpaid leave?
leo-ic: I also want to confirm if being on leave pauses my 401k/benefit eligibility or changes my vesting outcome. Don't want surprises.
elaine-peopleops: Good edge case. Short answer: we can set the effective date to 11/01 and process retro for days worked/payable in the retro window. Unpaid leave days usually aren't paid, so retro pay will only cover pay-eligible days between 11/01 and the payroll run. For example if retro period is 11/01-11/14 but you are unpaid from 11/10-11/14, payroll will calculate retro only for 11/01-11/09.
zara-peopleops: Important to flag the leave on the comp change form and include LOA (leave of absence) approval docs. For a clean flow: 1) attach manager approval + calibration note 2) add LOA start/end in the Workday change comments 3) mark "retro pay requested" and list the exact retro range considering LOA days.
mike-engmgr: So if I ask for retro 11/01-11/14 but LOA covers 11/10-11/30 they'll only get retro for 11/01-11/09?
payroll-bot: Correct: payroll will only process retro for pay-eligible days in the window. LOA unpaid days are excluded from earnings. If you request retro covering LOA days, payroll will adjust and notify the requester of the final computed retro amount.
leo-ic: What about benefits and 401k contributions? If I'm unpaid for part of the month does that affect the months employer match or eligibility?
elaine-peopleops: Benefits eligibility effective dates are governed by plan rules. Many plans use the pay period or calendar month. If your LOA results in zero earnings for the payroll run, carrier eligibility might be affected — payroll will flag and benefits ops will coordinate with you. 401k deferrals require earnings to deduct from; employer match only applies to eligible deferrals during that run. If retro increases your earnings in that pay run (for the paid days), the deferrals/match for the retro period will be recalculated accordingly.
mike-engmgr: Does LOA change vesting or equity grant timing?
zara-peopleops: Vesting terms are per grant. Typically unpaid LOA may pause vesting depending on policy and local law — check the specific RSU grant language. Equity refreshes are separate approvals and have their own grant dates; level changes don't auto-issue refreshes. If vesting pause applies, equity ops will surface that.
leo-ic: If I return from LOA and my comp was processed as effective 11/01 with partial retro, are managers supposed to do any onboarding/check-ins?
\zela-peopleops: Managers should follow the promotion checklist regardless of LOA: schedule a post-promo check-in within 30 days of the effective date or within 30 days of return-to-work if LOA overlaps. Document outcomes in the growth doc and note LOA in the calibration record.
mike-engmgr: Any special approvals for LOA + retro?
elaine-peopleops: Add LOA approval docs to the HR case. If retro spans LOA we need HR signoff + payroll review. Also CC hr-escalations and payroll when submitting the Workday comp-change so payroll can proactively compute the pro-rated retro. Use subject: "Retro with LOA: [Employee] - effective 2026-11-01".
payroll-bot: Checklist before filing: 1) manager & director approval emails (PDF) 2) calibration excerpt/rubric (PDF) 3) LOA approval doc (PDF) 4) completed Workday comp-change marked "retro" with LOA dates in comments 5) email hr-escalations CC payroll. Cutoff reminder: changes must be approved by the 10th to affect the 15th run.
leo-ic: Thanks  that helps a lot. One last thing: will I see a separate line item for the retro adjustment on my paystub?
payroll-bot: Yes. Retro payments appear as separate earnings lines with the retro date range on the paystub. Tax and withholding will apply at the run level and may differ from the original pay period. If you have international tax questions, file a CRO with payroll ops.
mike-engmgr: Great, I'll collect the docs and flag LOA dates on the Workday form. Appreciate it :thumbsup:
zara-peopleops: Thanks team — ping us if you want a sample Workday note and we'll paste one.
